public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 540

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/540](https://www.erdosproblems.com/540)
- [Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on
  Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
- [Er73] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory*. A survey of combinatorial
  theory (Proc. Internat. Sympos., Colorado State Univ., Fort Collins, Colo., 1971) (1973), 117-138.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Ol68] Olson, John E., *An addition theorem modulo {$p$}*. J. Combinatorial Theory (1968), 45--52.
- [Ba12] Balandraud, Éric, *An addition theorem and maximal zero-sum free sets in
  $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$*. Israel J. Math. (2012), 405-429.
- [HaZe96] Hamidoune, Yahya Ould and Zémor, Gilles, *On zero-free subset sums*. Acta Arith. (1996),
  143--152.
- [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., *Unsolved problems in number theory*. (2004), xviii+437.
- [ErHe64] Erdős, P. and Heilbronn, H., *On the addition of residue classes
  mod $p$*. Acta Arith. (1964), 149--159.
- [Sz70] Szemerédi, E., *On a conjecture of Erdős and Heilbronn*. Acta Arith.
  (1970), 227-229.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos540

/-- A finite set has a non-empty subset whose sum is zero. -/
def HasZeroSubsetSum {G : Type*} [AddCommMonoid G] (A : Finset G) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Finset G, S ⊆ A ∧ S.Nonempty ∧ S.sum id = 0

/--
Is it true that if $A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ has size $\gg N^{1/2}$ then there exists
some non-empty $S\subseteq A$ such that $\sum_{n\in S}n\equiv 0\pmod{N}$?

Szemerédi proved the answer is yes, in fact for arbitrary finite abelian groups.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos540.lean"]
theorem erdos_540 : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
      ∀ (N : ℕ), 0 < N → ∀ A : Finset (ZMod N),
        C * Real.sqrt N ≤ A.card →
          HasZeroSubsetSum A := by
  sorry

end Erdos540

reformulations.difference: The source asks about |A| ≫ N^{1/2}. Erdős's wording is 'k > c n^{1/2}' / 'k > c√n' for distinct residues [Er65b p.230, Er73 §7], and Szemerédi's theorem [Sz70] only claims the strict bound |A| > c₀√n for n > n₀. The Lean statement instead says: there is some C > 0 such that the non-strict bound C·√N ≤ |A| gives a zero-sum subset for every N ≥ 1. N = 0 is excluded, so ZMod 0 ≃ ℤ never occurs. A may contain 0, whereas Erdős–Heilbronn 1964 used non-zero residues.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (⇒) Keep the constant and take n₀ = 0; a strict bound implies the non-strict one. (⇐) Suppose c > 0 and n₀ work with the strict bound for N > n₀. Take C = max(2c, √(n₀+1)). If 1 ≤ N ≤ n₀, then C√N ≥ √(n₀+1)·√N > N ≥ |A|, since |A| ≤ |ZMod N| = N. So no A meets the hypothesis. If N > n₀, then C√N ≤ |A| gives c√N < 2c√N ≤ |A|. Allowing 0 ∈ A changes nothing, because {0} is then a zero-sum subset. Proved in Lean as `fc_iff_sz : FCForm ↔ SzForm` (axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). `example : type_of% @Erdos540.erdos_540 = (True ↔ FCForm) := rfl` checks that the theorem's right-hand side is exactly FCForm.

review.notes:
The source and the file agree. erdosproblems.com/540 (page last edited 06 March 2026) asks: "Is it true that if A ⊆ ℤ/Nℤ has size ≫ N^{1/2} then there exists some non-empty S ⊆ A such that Σ_{n∈S} n ≡ 0 (mod N)?" It records the problem as PROVED (LEAN), with answer yes, by Szemerédi [Sz70], who proved it for all finite abelian groups. The file's docstring, `answer(True)`, `research solved` tag and `formal_proof` link match this.

Checks performed:
(1) `#print` shows the theorem is `True ↔ ∃ C, 0 < C ∧ ∀ N, 0 < N → ∀ A : Finset (ZMod N), C * √↑N ≤ ↑A.card → HasZeroSubsetSum A`, with both casts into ℝ.
(2) `HasZeroSubsetSum` behaves correctly on small cases, checked with `decide`: {1,2} in ZMod 5 has no zero-sum subset; {1,4} in ZMod 5 has one; {0} in ZMod 1 has one; ∅ has none; {1,2,3} has none in ZMod 7 but has one in ZMod 6.
(3) Degenerate cases: C > 0 rules out A = ∅; 0 < N rules out ZMod 0 = ℤ; N = 1 is fine.
(4) The formal_proof link checks out. The linked theorem `Erdos540.erdos_540` in plby/lean-proofs states the same claim; its `hasZeroSum` only adds an unused `[DecidableEq G]` argument. The file targets Lean/Mathlib v4.29.1 and fails verbatim under this repository's v4.33.1 in three places, all simp-set drift. After three one-line patches it compiles, `#print axioms` lists only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], and it proves the repository's exact `erdos_540` type.

Minor, non-mathematical observations:
- The formal_proof URL points to the `main` branch, not a pinned commit.
- The source's remarks are not formalised as variants: the conjectured sharp threshold (2N)^{1/2} (Erdős/Selfridge), the prime-N results of Olson and Balandraud, and the Hamidoune–Zémor bound (1+o(1))√(2N). Leaving them out is an omission, not a misformalization.
